BiblicalUsage: zaʻăvâh means agitation, maltreatment. In Deuteronomy 28:25 we read, "The LORD shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them..." It appears again in 2 Chronicles 29:8: "Wherefore the wrath of the LORD was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment..."
TheologicalSignificance: za'avah is agitation, maltreatment, and I hold that God teaches through ordinary words as well as great ones.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
